title: Token Burst Forensics and Debugging Workflow
author: Mariana Ortega
content:
Overview:
This page documents the downstream debugging workflow for sudden token bursts (large unexpected per-minute token consumption) observed on the Redwood platform. It is intended for on-call platform operators and SREs who must triage cost-surge alerts, restore predictable billing and performance, and gather forensic evidence for post-incident analysis.

Goal and scope:
- Restore customer-facing traffic within 30 minutes for P0 token-burst incidents.
- Contain cost exposure to the threshold defined by the regional cost-guard policy (default: $10k/hour global excess).
- Produce a short RCA and action items within 48 hours.
- Scope: hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, and edge routing layers that can trigger token-rate changes (rate-limiters, batching, mirror traffic).

Key signals and detection sources:
1) Alerts (primary):
   - grafana-alert: token-rate-excess-high (threshold: tokens_per_minute > 1.5x historical 99th percentile for 15m)
   - billing-alert: token-cost-spike (billing pipeline detects 5x hourly cost delta)
   - sla-warn: model-latency-degradation (tokens and latency coupled)
2) Telemetry tables and queries:
   - metrics.tokens.ingested_per_min (series by tenant, region, model, route)
   - traces.request.token_budget_used (span attribute)
   - logs.api.requests (request_id, tenant_id, prompt_length, model_id, tokens_out, stream_flag)
3) Canary dashboards to check immediately:
   - Live token heatmap (tenant x region x last 60m)
   - Per-model token distribution (P50/P90/P99 prompt_length)

Immediate containment checklist (0–15 minutes):
1) Acknowledge the alert and assign the incident lead (operator-sre).
2) If billing exposure is immediate: enable global temporary token hard cap by calling the cost-guard API:
   - curl -X POST https://platform-control.internal/api/v1/cost-guard/activate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_KEY' -d '{"scope":"global","cap_type":"hard","cap_value":"1000000"}'
3) Apply tenant-level throttle for the top 3 tenants by token rate:
   - Identify top tenants: SELECT tenant_id, sum(tokens) FROM metrics.tokens.ingested_per_min WHERE ts > now() - interval '60 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY sum DESC LIMIT 3;
   - Apply throttles via admin CLI: rcli tenant throttle set --tenant <tenant_id> --rate 1000 --window 60s
4) If a single model shows anomalous token amplification (e.g. tool-calling loop), disable the model routing and fallback to a safe variant:
   - rcli routing set --route <route_id> --model fallback-safety-1
5) Communicate an initial incident note on #oncall-platform with summary and mitigation steps.

Triage and evidence collection (15–90 minutes):
1) Correlate tenants to API keys and recent deploys/releases:
   - Query deploy metadata: SELECT * FROM deploys WHERE tenant_id in (<list>) AND created_at > now() - interval '24 hours';
2) Inspect sampling logs for amplified prompts:
   - Search logs for prompt templates containing evidence of loops (keywords: "repeat", "append", "tool_call", "function_call"), and track average tokens_out per request.
   - Example log grep: grep -R "tool_call" /var/logs/api/requests | jq '. | {request_id, tenant_id, tokens_out, model_id, timestamp}' | head -n 50
3) Use tracing to follow a high-token request end-to-end:
   - Open Jaeger trace for request_id and review child spans for external tool calls or repeated requeues.
4) Identify automated clients / bots:
   - Detect large numbers of requests with identical user-agent or with no session identifiers.
   - Query: SELECT user_agent, count(*) FROM logs.api.requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '60 minutes' GROUP BY user_agent ORDER BY count DESC 
5) Check batching and KV-cache behavior for regen storms: confirm if continuous batching caused repeated kv cache misses due to dynamic prefixes.

Containment options (choose per root cause):
- Errant client / runaway loop: block API key and force rotate; apply tenant throttle; coordinate with CS for customer contact.
- New model rollout causing amplification: rollback the model or pin the route to previous version.
- Internal replay or mirrored traffic: disable mirroring for affected routes and apply circuit-breaker.
- Cache eviction / sharding bug: apply emergency warmup script to prefill prefix caches for hot tenants and reduce batching window.
- Billing pipeline false-positive: validate with raw usage export and correct metric source.

Operator commands and scripts (approved operator tools):
- rcli token-usage tail --tenant <id> --minutes 60  # real-time tail of token series
- rcli tenant throttle set --tenant <id> --rate <rpm> --window 60s
- rcli routing set --route <route> --model <model_id> --reason "emergency-mitigation"
- admin-console: /operator/controls/cost-guard (UI path)

Investigation checklist (90m–4h):
1) Produce a compact event timeline (CSV) with columns: ts, tenant_id, route, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, action_taken.
2) Export raw request payloads for 50 representative high-token requests and store under /incident-artifacts/<incident-id>/requests.csv (access controlled).
3) Compare token composition: prefix_tokens v.s. generated_tokens v.s. tool_tokens.
4) If a third-party tool call loop is observed, capture the external call graph (URL, headers, rate) and notify Security if exfiltration or abuse is suspected.
5) Confirm cost attribution mapping (billing_tag -> tenant) to avoid misattribution.

Dashboard and alert tuning recommendations (post-incident):
- Introduce a short-window (1m) high-sensitivity alert and a longer-window (30m) stability alert to reduce false positives.
- Add alert enrichment to include top-3 tenants and top-3 models in the alert body. Example grafana alert annotation:
  - Summary: "Token surge: 1.5x 99p (15m)"
  - Details: "Top tenants: t-123 (45%), t-456 (12%), t-789 (6%) | Top models: gpt-x-safety-v2 (62%)"
- Create a synthetic test that simulates a 2x prompt-length amplification to validate throttles and routing fallbacks in staging.
- Add a panel showing per-tenant sudden-increase-velocity (delta% over baseline) with color thresholds (amber at 50%, red at 200%).

Roles & ownership matrix:
- Incident lead: operator-sre (rotating oncall) — triage and mitigation authority.
- Billing lead: finance-eng — validate costs and engage cost-guard controls.
- Product/Support liaison: customer_success — customer outreach and post-incident communication.
- Runtime engineer: eng-serving-runtime — investigate model/kernel causes, KV cache, and batching behavior.

Post-incident actions (within 48 hours):
1) Short RCA (one pager) with timeline, root cause, impact (tenants, estimated excess cost), remediation actions, and owners.
2) Implement at least one mitigation within 7 days (e.g., throttle-by-default for new tenants, token budget gate for new routes).
3) Add a regression test in the platform CI: simulate a 1000x small-request storm and assert cost-guard activation within configured window.
4) Update runbook sections or create new alert pages if the incident uncovered an instrumentation gap.

Retrospective template (to run in the 1-week postmortem meeting):
- What happened? (2–3 slides)
- Why did our controls fail to prevent this? (instrumentation, default configs, process)
- What went well? (fast containment, clear comms)
- Action items (owner, due date, priority)
- Follow-ups: schedule a cross-team design review if model rollout or client SDK changes were root cause.

Appendix A — Sample quick queries and exports:
- Top routes by token:
  SELECT route, sum(tokens_out) as tokens FROM metrics.tokens.ingested_per_min WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 minutes' GROUP BY route ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 10;
- Suspected loop detection (identical prompt hash, high tokens):
  SELECT prompt_hash, count(*) as hits, avg(tokens_out) FROM logs.api.requests WHERE ts > now() - interval '60 minutes' GROUP BY prompt_hash HAVING hits > 20 AND avg(tokens_out) > 5000 ORDER BY hits DESC;

Appendix B — Logging and retention notes:
- Preserve all raw logs and exported requests for 90 days under incident retention policy; longer if legal review is required.
- Ensure artifacts are stored with RBAC applied: incident-artifacts are only visible to incident participants and Security.

Appendix C — Example incident stub (for copy/paste into Slack):
- [INCIDENT] Token Burst (P0) — observed 2026-02-18T03:12Z
- Summary: tokens_per_min across hosted-api increased 6x; top tenant t-123 responsible for 48% of spike; initial mitigation: tenant throttle and model rollback.
- Actions taken: cost-guard activated, top tenants throttled, routing pinned to fallback-safety-1.
- Next update: +30m — operator-sre
